deities: Kalbhairav (Kal Bhairav, fierce form of Shiva)

history.period: 18th century (complex built 1713–1738 CE; shrine-specific date unverified)
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE (verify): web sources confirm the Shri Shantadurga Temple complex at Kavlem comprises one main temple and three smaller subsidiary temples of other deities, but none of the consulted sources individually name Kalbhairav among the three. This file documents the Kalbhairav subsidiary shrine named in the CSV, which is almost certainly one of those three smaller temples. The parent complex: the Shantadurga deity (also called Santeri, the mediator between Vishnu and Shiva) was shifted from Quelossim (Keloshi) in Salcete after the Portuguese destroyed the original temple in the 1560s; the present complex was built during the Maratha reign of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara (1713–1738), with the village of Kavalem bequeathed to the temple by Baji Rao I Peshwa in 1738 through Naroram Mantri. The complex follows Indo-Portuguese temple architecture with pyramidal shikharas, a flat dome, Roman-arched windows, a huge tank, a deepa stambha and agrashalas. The shrine's own founding date is UNVERIFIED — no source dates it separately from the complex. The media image shows the Shantadurga temple complex, not the Kalbhairav shrine specifically (no dedicated image of the shrine was found).

name: Kalbhairav shrine, Shantadurga temple complex
town_description: Kavlem (also spelled Kavalem) is a village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, set in the foothills of the Western Ghats about 30 km from Panaji. It is Goa's best-known temple cluster, home to the Shantadurga, Nagesh, Ramnath, Mahalasa Narayani and Laxmi Narayan temples, most of them relocated here from Portuguese-held Salcete during the 16th–18th centuries. The village's economy and identity revolve around its temples, agrashalas (pilgrim guest houses) and pilgrim services.
